claims.text: The as-built Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The as-built alloy has demonstrated high strength and fatigue resistance.
High-temperature degradation is controlled by the formation and stability of a protective Cr/Ti-rich oxide scale.
An oxidizing atmosphere produces a continuous and adherent oxide scale on the alloy.
The oxide scale formed in an oxidizing atmosphere limits further oxidation and degradation.
A reducing atmosphere produces an incomplete, less-protective, or spallation-prone oxide scale.
Scale disruption in a reducing atmosphere leads to increased internal oxidation and matrix degradation.
The relevant surface scale is predominantly enriched in Cr and Ti and may contain Cr2O3 and TiO2.
Cr and Ti selectively oxidize under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Ti forms a coherent, adherent oxide layer.
A coherent Cr/Ti-rich scale limits oxygen diffusion into the underlying fcc matrix.
In reducing conditions, the oxide may be partially reduced and become prone to spallation.
Greater oxygen ingress in reducing conditions causes internal oxidation and deleterious microstructural changes.
At about 700°C for 100 hours, the oxidizing atmosphere will yield a thin, uniform, adherent Cr/Ti-rich scale with minimal matrix degradation.
At about 700°C for 100 hours, the reducing atmosphere will yield disrupted or thinner oxide coverage and greater internal oxidation.
Specimens exposed to the reducing atmosphere will show greater mechanical-property degradation than specimens exposed to the oxidizing atmosphere.
A post-fabrication stress-relief treatment removes residual thermal stresses.
The protective role of Cr/Ti-rich oxide scales is well established in simpler alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The reducing exposure is specified as 5% H2 in N2 with no oxygen-bearing component, yet the mechanism predicts greater oxygen ingress and internal oxidation under that condition without identifying an oxygen source or residual oxygen potential.

The baseline is defined as the as-manufactured state, but specimens may optionally receive stress relief before exposure. This creates an ambiguous starting state and could confound comparison with the stated as-manufactured baseline.
